owner_request: Proposed towns should not dwarf the nearby marked (lore) settlement; the model should take this into account inherently, not by post-hoc swaps.
evidence_seen_before_declaration: Roman AD 150 cohort (664 towns, Greek walls at inhabited share), descriptive only: of 95 towns within 75 km of a provincial capital, 6.3% are larger than it (median size ratio 0.11); 30% of towns are the largest within 75 km; non-dominant towns have median size 0.27 x their local maximum (quartiles 0.12-0.49).

model_H.idea: Sizes are generated as a settlement hierarchy. Centres are drawn first (on the map: the marked campaign places, in lore order, with the capital term; on Earth: the provincial capitals). Every other town draws its size relative to its centre: ln area_u = ln area_c + delta, with delta from an Earth-fitted conditional model delta = d0 + d1 (lnH_u - lnH_c) + d2 distance + scatter, fitted on Roman towns within 75 km of a centre. Towns farther than 75 km from any centre keep the M1C draw.
model_H.ceiling: No hard cap: the fitted delta distribution decides how often a subordinate town exceeds its centre (6% on Earth near capitals).

validation_declared: Province-blocked folds on the Roman cohort with capitals as centres: held-out (1) share of subordinate towns larger than their centre within 75 km, (2) median size ratio to the centre, (3) whole-cohort KS and total-area ratio as the size gate (KS <= 0.10, ratio 0.80-1.25). Pass if (3) passes and (1), (2) are within 0.05 and a factor 1.25 of the observed. A generator that passes is applied on the map with marked places as centres (owner rule: lore order among marked places stays binding).
caveat: On the map, centres include imperial forts, monasteries and fortified towns, a wider set than Roman provincial capitals; a fortified town is a weaker centre. The fit can include centre class only where Earth evidence exists (capitals); other marked classes are treated as centres by owner rule.

amendments.made_after: scoring the declared delta form (kept as results_delta_form.json): KS 0.096 and area ratio 1.04 pass, but share of subordinates larger than their centre 12.6% vs observed 6.3% and median ratio 0.082 vs 0.11 fail; M1C alone gives 21.5% and 0.37
amendments.known: The delta form models y_u - y_c; its scatter (sd 1.75) mixes the subordinate's and the centre's residuals, so generating it on top of an already drawn centre double-counts the centre's randomness.
amendments.change: Conditional form: ln area_u = g0 + g1 ln area_c + g2 lnH_u + g3 distance/100 + scatter, fitted on subordinates (centre size observed as a predictor), generated given the generated centre. Same folds, seeds, metrics and pass rule. Development data; post-hoc reformulation disclosed.

amendments.made_after: scoring the A1 conditional form (kept as results_conditional_form.json: 31% of subordinates larger than their capital, median ratio 0.52, fail) and a diagnostic of held-out M1C residuals by distance from capitals
amendments.known: Subordinate size does not follow centre size (coefficient -0.19), and towns near capitals are not smaller than M1C predicts (mean held-out residual -0.12 to +0.03 within 75 km; no shadow). With independent residuals M1C gives 21% of subordinates larger than their capital vs 6% observed.
amendments.change: Centre selection (order statistic): each centre and the towns assigned to it (nearest centre within 75 km) form a cluster; residual draws are generated as before, and the centre takes the largest residual of its cluster (the town that drew it takes the centre's). Means (M1C, with each town's own hinterland and the capital term) are unchanged. Same folds, seeds, metrics and pass rule; post-hoc reformulation on development data, disclosed.

amendments.made_after: scoring A2 (kept as results_selection_with_capital_term.json): 0% of subordinates larger than their capital, median ratio 0.057 (overshoot)
amendments.known: The M1C capital term was fitted on observed capital sizes, which already contain the selection effect; selection on top of it double-counts.
amendments.change: Selection alone: means from the published M1 refit WITHOUT a capital term (1.915 + 0.147 lnH, held-out sigma 1.048; fold coefficients refitted on the same folds), residuals generated as before, each centre takes the largest residual of its cluster. Also reported: the implied capital factor (mean generated ln area of capitals minus the M1 mean) against the observed 3.4x. Same pass rule.

amendments.made_after: scoring A3 (kept as results_selection_only.json): implied capital factor 1.99 vs observed 3.22, 1.3% of subordinates larger than their capital vs 6.3%, median ratio 0.17 vs 0.11; A2 (selection + full capital term) overshot
amendments.known: Full selection plus the observed capital term overshoots; selection alone undershoots. The truth lies between.
amendments.change: Two-parameter centre model: ln area_c = M1 mean + c + sigma x (largest of the centre's own residual and those of a fraction phi of its cluster, the cluster members taken in a fixed seeded order); subordinates keep their own M1 draws (the member whose residual the centre took receives the centre's). phi in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1}, c in {0.0, 0.1, ..., 1.3}. For each held-out fold, (phi, c) minimises on the three training folds the sum of squared differences of (share of subordinates larger than their centre, ln median ratio, ln capital factor) between generated (5 seeds) and observed; the held-out fold is then generated with them. Pass rule on the pooled held-out generation unchanged (KS, area ratio, share within 0.05, median ratio within x1.25), plus implied capital factor within x1.25 of observed.
